name: Home Cooks DXB
about: Recipes from our kitchens in Dubai: weeknight dinners, family classics, sourdough disasters and the occasional spice-cabinet rescue.

posts.author: p03
posts.text: Sourdough disaster log, week three: my starter smelled like nail polish remover, then I discovered it was just hungry. Feed it twice a day and it's a different animal.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Nail polish smell means it's hungry, yes. Feed it at room temperature and it recovers quickly.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Layla the pastry chef struggling with sourdough, I'm so entertained. Keep going!

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Feeding twice a day is the rule. Also keep the jar loosely covered so the gas escapes.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: My starter also smelled like paint thinner once. It got better after a week of feeding.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Sourdough is a long relationship. You will both learn patience, I promise.

comments.author: p09

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Question for the home cooks: what is the easiest way to get a decent bowl of pho at home? I have the broth ingredients but not the time for a twelve hour simmer.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Pressure cooker is your friend. Ninety minutes gives a deep broth, not a perfect one but close.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Toast the onion and ginger first. That step alone makes the broth taste like a long simmer.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Star anise and cinnamon in small amounts, the secret is restraint. Don't overdo it.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Use good beef bones and roast them first, the colour and flavour are better.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Fish sauce is the secret umami, a tablespoon at the end. Trust me, you'll see.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Clear broth needs a gentle simmer, not a boil. The pressure cooker can be too aggressive.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy is not allowed broth with onion, so I'm watching the pho from a distance, sadly.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Post-run pho is a dream, I need to try this. Noodles are the easy part.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Rice noodles from the store, cooked just before serving. Don't soak them too long.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @anjali_rao the pressure cooker tip is great. I'll try it on Friday with the beef.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Keep the herbs fresh on the side, Thai basil and bean sprouts, the finishing touch.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Lime, chilli, and hoisin on the table, let everyone customise. Good for a group dinner.

comments.author: p07

comments.author: p01

comments.text: Coffee grounds and chocolate are also not for dogs, I learned that from a vet friend.

comments.author: p04

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Spice cabinet rescue: my cumin, coriander and turmeric have been in the cupboard since I moved in. Tips on when to replace them, and how to store them so they stay bright?

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ground spices lose their punch after about six months. Whole spices last much longer.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Store them away from heat and light, in a dark jar or tin. The kitchen counter is bad.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Buy whole spices and grind them when you need them. Huge difference in the flavour.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Test them by smelling. If the scent is weak, it's time to replace the jar.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: I keep the spice jars in a drawer, away from the oven. Simple, and the colour stays.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A quick toast in a dry pan wakes up old spices, though the flavour is never the same.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy has been eating the cumin dust from the floor, so please keep the jars sealed.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Label the jars with the purchase date, it's the easiest way to track freshness.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Good tip. I'll replace the turmeric, it's been in my cupboard since the last summer.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @ravi_menon yes, turmeric fades fast. Buy a small jar, you'll use it up quicker.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Buy from shops with high turnover, the spices are fresher. Ask the seller how often they restock.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: The Deira spice market is a great place to buy fresh spices in small amounts.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Deira spice souk is a sensory feast. Bring your nose and a small bag.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee beans and spices in the same cupboard? Please, keep them apart, the aroma travels.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good point, Yusuf. Smell transfer is real, especially with coffee.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Clean the spice jars and dry them well, moisture makes them clump quickly.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy supports the new spice rules. He prefers the bowl of water on the counter.

comments.author: p09
